title: Seahaven embeddings + rerank architectural walkthrough
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranker endpoints. Covered API flows, console observability, Optimize recommendations for batching/caching, and security questions (SOC2, SSO, VPC options). Agreed pilot: 2-week relevance pilot with sample logs, Redwood to send pricing + SOW.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Miles Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Aisha Malik (Seahaven Head of Search), Tom Bowers (Seahaven Eng Manager), Natalie Ruiz (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto): Demo & architectural Qs; pilot agreed pending pricing and sample logs.

[00:00] Miles: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Miles from Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:06] Aisha: good thanks Miles. excited to see the reranker flow — we've been dealing with noisy results from our existing vector search, want to understand how Redwood's hosted endpoints fit into our stack.
[00:14] Priya: great, we'll do an end-to-end. quick agenda: embeddings API, the reranker endpoint, console observability + the Optimize suggestions for batching and quant, then security and pilot scope.
[00:24] Tom: sounds good. just to set context, our stack is: Postgres + a scaled vector index (FAISS) in GCP, requests come from a python microservice. importance: sub-150ms p95 for search path and tight cost targets.
[00:38] Miles: perfect. high level — hosted mode means you use Redwood's API for embeddings and rerank. we'll show live requests but this is a conceptual walkthrough.
[00:46] Priya: starting with embeddings — call /v1/embeddings, send text or batched texts. we showed our sample python snippet; we also support streaming and chunked uploads. latency is highly dependent on batch size and model choice.
[00:57] Natalie: do you support custom fine-tuned embed models or only curated open models?
[01:02] Priya: we primarily surface curated open models with performance profiles, but for customers we can onboard specific models — there is an onboarding path (SE-assisted) and then you can pin that model in your project. sometimes the transcript says "model on boarding" which is slow — but it's a formal process.
[01:18] [01:18] Miles: now reranker — we have a dedicated rerank endpoint that takes the query, candidate docs (IDs + content or precomputed embeddings), and returns a score + explain tokens if you request structured outputs. this is server-side reranking so you don't have to re-rank client-side with LLMs.
[01:33] Tom: can we pass our FAISS candidate IDs and have Redwood fetch our doc bodies or do we need to include full content?
[01:39] Priya: good question. two options: include full text in the request (simpler), or include doc IDs and a fetch hook where you host content and we call back (webhook) — that second flows needs an allowlist and minimal latency budget.
[01:52] Aisha: latency — our ops team is very strict. what's typical for rerank endpoint p95?
[01:58] Priya: for hosted reranker with default medium model and small candidate sets (top 10) p95 is ~80-160ms depending on load. we showed some perf profiles in the console during the call. note that using prefix caching / kv cache for repeated query prefixes can shave 20-40% off token compute.
[02:16] Natalie: prefix cache? you mean the KV cache — like cached KV states for autoregressive decoders? can you explain.
[02:23] Priya: yes — our runtime supports KV cache reuse for repeated tokens across sessions. for rerank we often use short context lengths but if you have repeated boilerplate we can cache. sometimes transcription shows K-V "cash" which is funny.
[02:34] [02:34] Miles: jump into the console — Priya shared screen (demo). dashboard shows per-route token breakdown, cost per call, latency histograms, and model variant fallback events. you can set rollout policies: canary to a quantized variant for cost vs accuracy checks.
[02:50] [03:01] Priya: Optimize suggestions screen recommends batching sizes per route, a quantization profile (8-bit or 4-bit) and indicates expected cost savings. for example, changing embeddings batch from 8->32 gave a 2.8x throughput improvement in our benchmark but increased median latency by ~30ms in that test.
[03:23] Tom: what's the recommended approach for read-heavy search traffic? bigger batches? or aggressive caching?
[03:28] Priya: mix: large async batchers for embeddings ingestion and memoized prefix caching + small synchronous batches for query-time rerank. Optimize will suggest exact batch size and queueing thresholds based on measured latency SLOs.
[03:40] Aisha: security — we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, audit logs, and ideally an option where inference data doesn't persist beyond processing. can Redwood do that?
[03:49] Miles: yes. hosted mode supports ephemeral storage for inference payloads, SOC2 Type II, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and we can do contract language around data retention. for stricter requirements we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) which you run in your cloud account.
[04:05] Natalie: question on embeddings alignment — we've seen embedding drift when switching models. does Redwood provide tools to compare embedding spaces or run evals?
[04:13] Priya: yes, the Console has an Eval suite where you can run a relevance test set — compute MRR/NDCG for different model/quantization choices. Optimize ties regression alerts to those evals so when a rollout changes quality you'll see signals.
[04:29] [04:29] Miles: they asked about fallbacks. our routing supports model variant chain: if the primary model is unavailable we can fallback to a cheaper variant or a different region automatically — you can set soft/ hard SLOs.
[04:42] Tom: cost — how granular is pricing? we want token-level breakdown and per-route allocations to chargeback to product teams.
[04:49] Miles: Console exposes token cost by model and by route; we can also surface per-customer or per-team allocations. we'll include a sample billing export for your finance team.
[04:59] Natalie: onboarding effort — how quickly could we run a 2-week pilot?
[05:03] Miles: quickly. typical pilot: share anonymized search logs, Redwood runs a baseline embedding + rerank test and produces a benchmark report. timeline 1 week to set up, 1 week for evaluation + tuning.
[05:12] Aisha: perfect. any blockers on our side?
[05:15] Priya: we'll need a sanitized sample of search queries & clicks, a small subset of documents, and a short list of target metrics (p95 latency, desired MRR uplift).
[05:24] [05:24] Miles: quick demo note — we did a live rerank call: sent query + 8 candidates, reranker returned scores + a short JSON explain. there was a slight audio glitch and the transcript auto-labeled an utterance as "Speaker 1" when it was Priya.
[05:40] Tom: i noticed the console traces — are those trace IDs exportable to our internal tracing system?
[05:45] Priya: yes, we support trace hooks and you can ingest spans into your existing tracing tool via a small shim.
[05:52] Aisha: about VPC/private — are there recurring infra fees? how does billing work for dedicated pools?
[05:58] Miles: Dedicated/reserved capacity has commit tiers (monthly/annual) and an infra baseline fee; Private in your VPC is licensed with a platform fee plus support. we'll include pricing options in the follow-up email.
[06:12] Natalie: one more technical — quantization: you mentioned 4-bit profiles. does that impact rerank quality?
[06:18] Priya: some models are quantization-friendly, others less so. Optimize runs a simulated quantization eval and gives an expected quality delta. for rerank we usually recommend testing 8-bit first then 4-bit on a small eval set.
[06:30] [06:30] Miles: ok let's recap and assign actions.
[06:33] Aisha: before that, one more: do you have any customers in media/publishing? is there an example case study?
[06:38] Miles: yes, couple — we'll share a redacted case study showing a 12% MRR uplift with hosted rerank. it'll be in the follow-up.
[06:45] Recap / Next Steps:
- Miles: send pricing + SOW options, redacted case study, security pack (SOC2, SAML config, data retention language).
- Priya: recording of the console demo, a runnable notebook that shows embeddings->FAISS->rerank example, and Optimize export with suggested batch sizes.
- Seahaven (Aisha/Tom/Natalie): share anonymized sample logs and a short list of target metrics, provision a test index or export candidates.

[06:58] Aisha: thanks, this was helpful. we'll aim to get logs to you by next week.
[07:02] Miles: great, thanks all. we'll follow up by email with the pilot SOW.

End of recording.
